implementation: Adapt Sloppy cd6ead0 affine-index decomposition and invariant arithmetic materialization. Guard the first/last unsigned indexes of a nonempty counter interval. Vectorize single checked counter-plus/minus-invariant indexes used only as memory indexes, shifting bases and retaining overlap guards. Use remaining distance for vector trip checks to avoid counter-plus-lanes overflow.
scope: No syntax changes, descending-loop lowering, extra global-load hoisting, or weakening of checked fallback semantics. Existing simple constant-offset recognition remains the first path. Added one permanent runtime workload, retaining the previous eight.

reference_stage.purpose: Fixed stage reference; do not replace with a slower implementation.

coverage: Native/WebAssembly default/release: shifted, invariant, and row-stride indexes; signed and unsigned endpoint overflow; valid wraparound; first failure after earlier effects.

Float32/float64 vector loops, both detected CPU features and forced SSE2; counts 0 through 17, negative and near-limit counters, addition/subtraction/commuted offsets, overlapping buffers requiring scalar execution, and index values also used as data.
Permanent shifted_arrays workload independently checks 2100736000 at count 1000 on native/web in both modes. All prior runtime workloads remain.

notes: The focused vector pilot uses C -O3 -march=native; the permanent stage suite preserves its established C -O2 reference. Those C ratios are separate measurements.
The scalar and first vector pilots precede the final independent C bootstrap. Toolchain hashes are retained for each.

A 4-bit exhaustive enumeration checks the interval guard implication in 139264 reduced-width cases; actual 64-bit native/web tests cover endpoint boundaries. This is a sanity check, not a formal proof.
The original record-release samples were inconclusive; retain them together with all 31 focused matched recheck pairs.
Compilation remains short of 250k fresh root lines/second; one fast vector workload does not establish broad C parity.
